messages:
emily: Customer "AcmeX" reporting auth failures only on Dedicated (VPC) deployment. Public hosted API works for them, dedicated endpoint returns 401 'invalid api key' for the same call. They say it started after switching to our LB in front of the dedicated pool. Repro steps they provided:

emily: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer123" \
  https://dedicated-acmex.redwood.example/api/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'

emily: When they hit the LB URL the curl shows the header present in the TLS handshake to the LB. But our backend logs show requests missing Authorization and failing at our auth layer. They see 200 when they hit a direct pod IP via port-forward.

sanjay: tagging eng-platform @alex and eng-infra @kai. Can someone check the LB/ingress and any sidecar that might strip Authorization?

alex: I tested a quick echo server behind the dedicated LB and reproduced. From my laptop hitting LB: Authorization present. From LB -> pod the header was absent. Repro commands I ran:

```bash
# from laptop (header visible to LB)
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer TEST123' https://dedicated-acme-test.redwood.example/echo

# then check backend (simple app logged headers)
kubectl logs deploy/echo -n dedicated-acme | tail -n 50
```

alex: backend log snippet: 

```
{"method":"GET","path":"/echo","headers":{}}
# no Authorization key at all
```

kai: Thanks. What is the LB type and any auth proxy in front? We have customers who add oauth2-proxy / auth-request sidecars that will intentionally consume Authorization or cookies.

emily: AcmeX uses an external oauth2 gateway (oauth2-proxy) in front of LB to do SSO for human traffic and it injects session cookie. They thought it was transparent for API calls. They also have an internal edge that rewrites headers for web requests.

sanjay: That rings a bell — oauth2-proxy has a config flag pass_access_token / pass_authorization_header behavior. If it's not configured, it may remove Authorization before passing upstream for security. Also some nginx configs set proxy_set_header Authorization "" to avoid leaking credentials.

alex: I checked the oauth2-proxy instance config (they shared via support ticket):

```yaml
# oauth2-proxy config snippet customer provided
provider: google
pass_basic_auth: false
pass_access_token: false
set_authorization_header: false
cookie_secure: true
```

alex: so oauth2-proxy intentionally does not forward Authorization. That matches our observation.

kai: Another wrinkle: if the LB uses TLS termination + re-encryption to backend, some proxies will drop Authorization when they see session cookies and assume web flow. But here oauth2-proxy is the culprit.

emily: Customer says they didn't realize oauth2-proxy would be in the path for programmatic API traffic. They expect the LB to forward all headers unchanged.

sanjay: Proposed fixes (ranked):
1) If they want upstream to receive the original Authorization header, enable pass_access_token / set_authorization_header in oauth2-proxy and restart. Example: set_authorization_header: true and pass_access_token: true.
2) Alternatively move API routes to a distinct L7 path/host that bypasses oauth2-proxy (common pattern: /api/* goes straight to backend).
3) If using nginx/ingress, ensure config doesn't clear Authorization (check for proxy_set_header Authorization "").
4) As a short-term workaround, accept an X-Forwarded-Authorization header and map it to Authorization in our dedicated gateway, but that's a security tradeoff.

alex: I tested locally by turning on set_authorization_header: true and pass_access_token: true in oauth2-proxy and the echo server started receiving Authorization again. Logs after change:

```
# backend log after config change
{"method":"GET","path":"/echo","headers":{"authorization":"Bearer TEST123","x-forwarded-for":"35.18.12.3"}}
```

kai: For customers on Istio: there's an extra gotcha with ext_authz. If you're using Istio external auth, the ext_authz filter can consume the header during token introspection if not configured to forward it. Check Envoy ext_authz config: `allowed_authorization_headers` must include Authorization or the header will be removed.

emily: Customer also uses Istio on their side and they had an external auth cluster configured for SSO. They attached the ext_authz config snippet to the ticket. It had no allowed_authorization_headers defined.

alex: sample Envoy ext_authz config that strips headers by default: 

```yaml
http_filters:
- name: envoy.filters.http.ext_authz
  typed_config:
    '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.ext_authz.v3.ExtAuthz
    http_service:
      server_uri:
        uri: http://authz.svc.cluster.local:8080
      authorization_request:
        allowed_headers:
          patterns:
          - exact: cookie
          - exact: x-requested-with
      authorization_response:
        allowed_upstream_headers:
          patterns:
          - exact: x-auth-user
```

alex: In that snippet Authorization is not allowed through. You need to include Authorization (and maybe Cookie) in `authorization_response.allowed_upstream_headers` if the auth service returns headers, and `authorization_request.allowed_headers` must allow Authorization if original token should be forwarded to auth service.

kai: Steps we recommended to the customer:
- For oauth2-proxy front: enable set_authorization_header: true & pass_access_token: true OR route API traffic to bypass oauth2-proxy.
- For Istio/Envoy ext_authz: update config to explicitly allow Authorization header in allowed_headers/allowed_upstream_headers.
- Check LB/nginx config for any proxy_set_header Authorization "" lines and remove them.
- Reproduce with echo endpoint and share backend logs.

emily: Customer applied `set_authorization_header: true` and restarted oauth2-proxy. They reported immediate success — 200s returned and our auth layer accepted the token. They also plan to add a dedicated API hostname that bypasses the oauth2-proxy for programmatic clients.

kai: Leaving a note for infra: consider documenting the common oauth2-proxy + Istio ext_authz header caveats in our dedicated deployment checklist. I will open a follow-up doc.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-921 - Dedicated VPC: auth header forwarding with oauth2-proxy (low-sev)

emily: closing the support ticket with the customer after validation. Marking as resolved on our side. :white_check_mark:

sanjay: Thanks everyone. TL;DR - header was consumed/blocked by oauth2-proxy + ext_authz config; fix by enabling forward flags or bypassing the proxy for API traffic.
